docs.owned.component: `Owned` names the BOX an element came from. It is the reference "return the strays" reads —
`reconcile` sends every piece back to its box — and the field a rule reaches as `el.box`: a
return-slot that takes only its own deck's cards, a scoring rule that counts only your pieces.
// a slot that returns red-deck cards reads it through the rule language:
The box is where the element BELONGS, not where it sits: a red-deck card on the desk, in a hand
or in the discard still answers `redDeck`. An empty box is a missing fact — a rule comparing
`el.box` denies, exactly as any missing operand does.
docs.owned.box: One card, two return-slots. Each slot takes only cards of its own box — `el.box` in the rule
reads this very atom. Flip `box` and drag: the matching slot lights, the other stays dark, and
nothing else about the card changed — the box is a name it carries, not where it sits.
